issue.title: sase bead doctor --fix-design-refs takes ~2 hours for 456 beads because it updates and flushes one bead at a time
issue.description:
Proposed by phase bead sase-ky.3 (epic sase-ky, plan @plan:202608/plan_ref_kind_rename.md) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on 2026-08-13T21:01:10Z; filed by sase-ky.land after search and the one-week task sweep found no duplicate (sase-f9 is about CLEARING stale design/artifact refs, not about the apply path's cost).

REPRODUCTION: running 'sase bead doctor --fix-design-refs' on this machine's bead store to migrate the legacy plans: design-ref spelling to plan: correctly repaired 456 event-backed design references but took roughly two hours of wall clock to do it.

ROOT CAUSE: src/sase/bead/cli_admin.py:99-103 applies the repairs with a per-bead loop -- 'for repair in preview.repairs: mutation.project.update(repair.bead_id, design=repair.new_reference)' -- inside a single bead_store_mutation. Each update writes its own event and flushes its own projection change, so the cost is 456 sequential write/flush round trips rather than one batched write. The existing batch path does not help here: 'sase bead update' accepts several bead IDs but applies the SAME field values to all of them, whereas a design-ref repair needs a different design value per bead.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the supported migration path for legacy design references, and it is the only one. A two-hour foreground run is long enough that an agent will be killed, interrupted, or will work around it, and any future ref-kind or bead-ID migration touching the whole store pays the same cost. sase-ky.3 had to babysit it to completion.

SCOPE: add an apply path that writes N differing per-bead design values in one batched store mutation -- one event append and one projection flush for the whole repair set -- and route --fix-design-refs through it. Note this likely crosses the Rust core boundary: 'mutation.project.update' is the core-backed bead update, so the batched-heterogeneous-update API probably belongs in ../sase-core/crates/sase_core with a new binding and wire, with cli_admin.py as the caller. Confirm first whether an existing core batch primitive can already take per-item field values before adding one. Cover with a test that the repair set is applied atomically and that a mid-run failure leaves no partial projection, and record the before/after timing on a store of comparable size.
